description: Shiitake is a choice edible wood-decay mushroom native to East Asia and one of the most widely cultivated mushrooms in the world, grown on hardwood logs and supplemented sawdust. It has a brown, often scaly cap, whitish gills, and a fibrous stem, and is valued both as food and for medicinal interest in its polysaccharide lentinan.
edibilityNotes: Choice edible only when thoroughly cooked. Eating raw or undercooked shiitake can cause shiitake (flagellate) dermatitis — a self-limiting but intensely itchy whip-lash/linear streak rash, typically appearing within 1-5 days of ingestion. It is attributed to lentinan, a heat-labile polysaccharide; thorough cooking degrades it and prevents the reaction. A minority of people may also experience digestive upset. Always cook shiitake fully before eating.
distribution: Native to warm, moist regions of East Asia (Japan, China, Korea) and Southeast Asia; now cultivated and consumed worldwide.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Omphalotus species (jack-o'-lantern)
dangerousLookalikes.note: Toxic jack-o'-lanterns are bright orange throughout with crowded, decurrent gills, grow in dense clusters on wood, and lack shiitake's brown scaly cap and white-ish adnexed gills. Wild brown-capped, gilled mushrooms on hardwood should be identified carefully before eating.
